decision: Memoize only a positive managed-runtime read; re-probe every inconclusive verdict

governingRule.description: A cached inconclusive probe must never suppress a later credential deny

alternativesConsidered.option: Memoize every verdict (as shipped): one child spawn per socket, but a managed VM that lost the socket startup race stays ambiguous for the whole process and an explicit host-gh opt-in then grants host credentials
Memoize non-managed verdicts behind a short TTL: keeps the spawn saving, but needs clock injection and makes the deny window a tuning parameter
Bounded re-probe budget per socket: still sticky once the budget is spent, so it only moves the failure later

whyWinner: A managed VM cannot stop being managed mid-process, so caching the deny is sound and keeps the memo's original purpose; every other verdict only says the API did not assert managed on that attempt, and re-probing costs a spawn bounded by the existing timeouts while caching one is unbounded in the fail-open direction
revisitTrigger: If ambiguous-runtime classification becomes hot enough that repeated child spawns show up in verb latency, add a short TTL with an injected clock rather than restoring an unbounded memo
